question: In a quadrilateral QRST, ∠Q = 96° and ∠R = 43°. The bisectors of ∠S and ∠T meet at E. What is the measure of ∠TES?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles in a quadrilateral equals half the sum of the remaining two interior angles.

⇒ ∠TES = (∠Q + ∠R) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TES = (96° + 43°) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TES = 139° ÷ 2 = 69.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 69.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In quadrilateral QRST, ∠Q = 96° and ∠R = 43°

SE and TE are the bisectors of ∠S and ∠T respectively.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S + ∠T = 360°

⇒ 96° + 43° + ∠S + ∠T = 360°

⇒ 139° + ∠S + ∠T = 360°

⇒ ∠S + ∠T = 360° − 139° = 221°

Now, in ΔSET, since SE and TE are bisectors of ∠S and ∠T:

⇒ ∠EST + ∠ETS = ∠S ÷ 2 + ∠T ÷ 2

⇒ ∠EST + ∠ETS = (∠S + ∠T) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠EST + ∠ETS = 221° ÷ 2 = 110.5°

Using the angle sum property in ΔSET:

⇒ ∠TES + ∠EST + ∠ETS = 180°

⇒ ∠TES + 110.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠TES = 180° − 110.5° = 69.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 69.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisectors of Opposite Angles

The angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two opposite angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the difference of the other two angles. Formula: θ = |∠B − ∠D| ÷ 2.

Sum of Angles of a Polygon

The sum of the interior angles of any n-sided polygon is calculated using the standard formula (n − 2) × 180°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

If all four vertices of a quadrilateral lie on the circumference of a circle, the opposite interior angles are supplementary, meaning they always sum to exactly 180°.
